source_identity.source_integrity_check: The evaluation checkpoint exactly matches the sealed C29 ACTIVE_WAVE row at the selection snapshot.

audited_claim.forward_only_versioning: Historical/no-contract, schema-v1 and schema-v2 replay_authorized histories use explicitly separated CLOSE bindings. Cross-version downgrade/upgrade is rejected.
audited_claim.torn_tail: In the injected harness, all 1,613 nonempty partial cuts of a replay-v3 CLOSE frame failed to become a reporting row and remained unresolved/torn-tail evidence.
audited_claim.scope: CLOSE/replay versioning preserves which pre-score runtime authorization predicate governed an attempt; it is not itself proof that model/scorer replay is deterministic.

v3_code.finding: The persisted source hard-codes exact sibling filenames/blobs for atomic journal, legacy reporting, historical/current-v1 auditors, v2 auditor and v2 registry. classify_admit_for_close distinguishes historical, current_v1, recognized replay_v2 and invalid/cross-version classes. select_replay_auditor then requires an exact matching reporting binding and raises on cross-version choices.
v3_code.scope: This is strong static support for the intended selection matrix.

registry_v2.finding: The persisted registry stores immutable canonical JSON for current-v1 and replay_authorized_v1 bindings; schema-v2 ADMIT resolution requires an allowlisted binding_id and exact binding digest. Unknown/invalid schema-v2 contracts return fail_closed. The replay-authorized binding includes the exact deterministic-replay-authorization facade blob.
registry_v2.scope: The registry materially prevents arbitrary caller-supplied runtime bindings from being accepted as replay authority.

validation_artifact.finding: The frozen validation records passed mixed historical/current-v1/schema-v2 replay, prepare_close restriction, v2 contract injection and explicit cross-version rejection. It also records binding digests and the accepted/rejected matrix.
validation_artifact.scope: The validation itself explicitly says it used contract-faithful test doubles and ran the pre-persistence candidate source, not the exact persisted Git blob plus full sibling graph.

scope_corrections.finding: The worker checkpoint and validation both explicitly state that blob 99c74f... was read back through the connector but not downloaded and byte-executed as that exact persisted blob in the local runtime.
scope_corrections.implication: Do not upgrade the injected validation to exact artifact execution. The persisted source is inspectable and structurally consistent, but exact execution readiness remains open.

scope_corrections.finding: Mixed-history and torn-tail harnesses used injected contract-faithful test doubles rather than the byte-materialized sibling runtime graph.
scope_corrections.implication: Failures caused by sibling import drift, dataclass/runtime details or real journal integration are not excluded by the current validation.

scope_corrections.finding: The new schema binds a deterministic-replay authorization facade before scoring, but no trusted deterministic LLM/scorer certificate is established in this checkpoint.
scope_corrections.implication: A replay_authorized_v1 ADMIT means the declared authorization predicate was selected, not that stochastic external calls are now scientifically identical across retries.

scope_corrections.finding: The 1,613 partial-cut result is persisted only as aggregate validation evidence; this audit did not independently regenerate the exact CLOSE frame and enumerate all cuts.
scope_corrections.implication: The fail-closed torn-tail claim is well scoped but remains worker-harness rather than fresh auditor byte-level reproduction.

scope_corrections.finding: The source records an accidental branch x created during capability probing, pointing to the frozen pre-semantic SHA and unused for semantic work.
scope_corrections.implication: It does not invalidate the source result, but demonstrates why connector capability discovery must remain read-only and is properly retained as an audit incident.

independent_replication.finding: This is an internal evaluation-runtime artifact, not a published external system. The auditor independently inspected the persisted source/registry logic but did not execute the full exact graph.

missing_dependencies_or_config.for_static_interpretation: The exact binding constants and registry resolution rules are persisted and sufficient for structural inspection.
missing_dependencies_or_config.for_exact_reproduction: Need byte-materialization of blob 99c74f... and all exact sibling blobs, then fresh-process execution of mixed histories plus crash/torn-tail cases. Deterministic external scorer/model replay remains a separate prerequisite.

o_specific_adaptation.finding: No O/O_FEED/O-derived state was used or tested; no claim is made that this runtime contract is deployed in O.

bottom_line: The forward-only runtime-provenance/CLOSE design is structurally strong and the persisted source makes cross-version fail-closed semantics inspectable. The key reproducibility boundary is exactly the one the worker records: validation used a source-equivalent candidate with test doubles, not byte-execution of the persisted v3 blob and frozen sibling graph. Therefore this is B+ implementation evidence, not yet an A-grade exact artifact replay. Replay authorization also remains distinct from proof of deterministic model/scorer behavior.
reopen_conditions: The exact v3 blob and all frozen sibling blobs are byte-executed in a clean runtime with mixed-history, crash/restart and torn-tail cases.
A replay-authorized top runtime is built and the active/default path changes from FAIL_CLOSED.
A trusted deterministic scorer/model certificate is added and tested against choose-among-retries behavior.
The runtime registry or CLOSE selection matrix changes materially.
exact_next_action: Do not repeat unchanged v3 injected validation. Reopen on exact sibling-graph execution or runtime/certificate changes; otherwise audit another exact ACTIVE_WAVE member.
